title: Lessons with Professor Nickerson and his daughter Camille
summary: Dejan started lessons around age nine or ten with Professor Nickerson, a violinist who taught all instruments; he recalls Camille Nickerson and Creole songs, and quit after about a year over outside music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, how old would you be, Hal, when you first picked up your... I'm not taking lessons around nine, ten years old. With the T.O.?
Yeah, I started with Professor Nickerson.
Is that the same piano teacher that Professor Minetta tells about?

Well, Professor Nickerson was a great violin player. Very wonderful violin player, but he taught all instruments. His daughter, Camille Nickerson, was a very fine pianist. She's in Howard University now, in Washington, I think. Well, I'd like to meet her. I'd like to meet her. She should remember, because she used to make me sing all them old Creole songs. When I was small, I knew all them songs. My mother used to learn them to me, you know, Creole songs. And I used to say she'd play them on the piano.
Now, he'd be an old gentleman at that time.
Oh, yeah, he was an old man. He had his goatees and his mustache, and they was white then. Torn and white, anyway, yeah.
Well, how long did you go to him for about that?
Oh, I went to him, I guess, about a year. Until he didn't like playing no outside music. So I would play what he taught.
